causal.assumptions_right: USD rates advantage versus CAD was real and funded the harvested win. USDCAD spot was the clean expression of that gap.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Treated leftover size as inexpensive peak-recapture optionality and underweighted three-digit oil as a CAD impulse that can stall USDCAD even with a 168bp front-end gap.
causal.causal_divergence: Core P&L came from harvesting the rates-gap trade. Residual risk was a 1.40/1.40 round trip because what remained was oil-and-event inventory, not the original rates gap.
causal.future_implication: Harvest-to-flat is mandatory on USDCAD after a material win when oil is three-digit. No reopen at 1.4028 this dual-CB week.
causal.observed_reality: Oil printed three-digit and is still there (WTI 101.76, Brent 115.81), Canadian impulse rose, and the leftover exited at the same 1.40 it was opened at, with Fed and BoC immediately ahead.
causal.original_belief: The SOFR-CORRA and UST-CAN 10Y gap would keep USDCAD bid, so a smaller leftover could recapture the prior peak without needing full size.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: Going fully flat when oil went three-digit and CAD impulse rose would have kept the realized win and avoided carrying remnant risk into Fed and BoC.

items.expression_assessment: Spot USDCAD was the right pair: both legs visible, no extra EUR or oil-beta cross. Expression was not the error.

facts.invalidation: Fed path recast as one-and-done and/or BoC/energy re-tightens CAD enough to close the policy gap.

items.future_rule: Do not leave a reduced USDCAD leftover waiting on peak recapture when oil is three-digit. Re-enter only if the desk would initiate from flat at the live print, and not into dual Fed/BoC week.
items.lesson: After a material USDCAD harvest, three-digit oil plus rising Canadian impulse means flatten fully.
items.sizing_assessment: Cutting down after the win was correct; not cutting to zero was the miss. Reduced leftover is not a free call on peak recapture.
items.thesis_assessment: Long USD versus CAD on the policy-rate and 10Y gap was directionally right and is why the trade paid. That thesis did not license leftover inventory once oil became a CAD impulse.
items.timing_assessment: The 19 Sep entry caught the rates gap. Holding the remnant into three-digit oil and the 28 Oct dual sitting was late. Exit at 1.40 closed the leftover without giving back the harvested core.
items.what_failed: A reduced leftover was left on to recapture a prior peak. It round-tripped 1.40 to 1.40 over about 36 days while oil went three-digit and Canadian impulse rose into Fed/BoC week.
items.what_worked: The USD-CAD rates gap paid. Expressing it in USDCAD spot, not a cross, let the core be harvested for a material realized gain.

causal.assumptions_right: Elevated U.S. yields did keep the dollar supported against the yen from 158.06 through 159.42. Verbal openness to a hike was not itself a hike, and the tape did not reverse on a policy event.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The exit treated openness to a hike as if it were the written invalidation. That underweighted the gap between a speech and a move in Japanese funding, and it used intervention as a reason to flatten without an intervention print.
causal.causal_divergence: The chain from a wide funding gap to a higher dollar-yen was still in force at 159.30. The position was removed by the timing of the flatten, not by the stop.
causal.future_implication: Dollar-yen stays off until a real policy, funding, or intervention event, or until a fresh breakout appears that the euro short and the franc long do not already express.
causal.observed_reality: The position was closed at 159.30. The next marks show 159.42, still not a breakout, the two-year at 4.80, and only an openness to a hike rather than a delivered one.
causal.original_belief: The long at 158.06 was meant to stay on while U.S. funding stayed restrictive and until the Bank of Japan actually hiked, funding converged, or intervention appeared.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: On the information at the exit, the rule was to keep the long until a hike, a funding convergence, or intervention printed. The next mark at 159.42 was a non-breakout, which argues for a smaller residual with the same stop, not for a new add.

facts.invalidation: The long is wrong if a later freeze shows the Bank of Japan hiking and TONA catching the March contract from the Japan side, or if official SOFR converges toward TONA so the overnight gap closes from the United States side. A Ministry of Finance intervention print that reverses the post-hold leftover also kills it. Three-digit oil is not this ticket's invalidation; it is why USDCAD stays flat.

items.future_rule: Keep a dollar-yen long until one of those three events prints. Do not reopen dollar-yen while the dollar length is already in the euro short and the franc long and the pair is not breaking out.
items.lesson: Do not close a dollar-yen long on hike rhetoric. The invalidation is a delivered hike with Japanese funding catching up, dollar funding converging, or intervention.
items.thesis_assessment: The rate-gap thesis was intact at the exit. The tactical case for staying long was thinner than the structural gap because dollar-yen had stopped breaking out, but the written stop had not printed.
items.what_failed: The long was closed before a delivered Bank of Japan hike, a funding convergence, or intervention. A governor who is open to a hike is not that invalidation, and 159.42 is still not a 20-day breakout.
items.what_worked: The dollar-yen long from 158.06 tracked a still-wide dollar funding gap. Spot was 159.30 at the exit and is 159.42 now, with the two-year at 4.80.

causal.assumptions_right: The assumption that the US path would stay above SOFR was right on the entry tape and is still right at a 4.85 ten-year. The dollar bid showed up more cleanly in euro at 1.0975 than in an incremental franc long.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The book underweighted that dollar-franc was already near a one-year high when the long was added beside the euro short. It also treated the three-part invalidation as the only exit, so a failed extension with the rate path still firm was held through the swing horizon.
causal.causal_divergence: The rate leg stayed restrictive and the franc leg failed to extend the 20-day upside break. The packet does not show the conjunction of a euro reclaim, a lost franc upside break, and a compressed US two-year premium.
causal.future_implication: A failed dollar-franc extension is an expression exit, separate from whether the US path remains above SOFR. The next dollar-franc long waits until the pair is no longer a one-year extreme and is no longer a second expression stacked on a live euro short.
causal.observed_reality: Dollar-franc was closed on 25 November and now prints 0.834 with a one-year z-score of 1.75, so the upside break did not extend. The US ten-year is 4.85 after a 22bp five-day rally, December Fed pricing is about 44bp, and SOFR is 3.94, so the US path stayed above the fixing.
causal.original_belief: The long dollar-franc was opened to ride an extension of the 20-day upside break. The US policy path was expected to stay above the SOFR fixing and keep the dollar bid against the franc.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same information, the franc long would have been skipped once dollar-franc was already near a one-year high and the euro short already carried the dollar rates bid. The same tape would have kept the dollar view in euro and cut dollar-franc when the 20-day break stopped extending.

items.expression_assessment: Dollar-franc was the second-order dollar vehicle. The euro short already carried the rates bid, and dollar-franc at a one-year z-score of 1.75 was the extended leg.

facts.invalidation: EURUSD reclaims its 20-day downside break and USDCHF loses its 20-day upside break while the US two-year premium over Europe and Japan compresses.

items.future_rule: Do not stack a fresh dollar-franc long on an existing euro short once dollar-franc is already near a one-year high. If the 20-day upside break stops extending while the US path remains above SOFR, close the franc leg even though the three-part invalidation has not printed.
items.lesson: Do not add dollar-franc when that pair is already near a one-year high and the dollar rates bid is already carried in a live euro short. A 20-day upside break that stops extending while the US path remains above SOFR is a failed extension and should be cut without waiting for the three-part invalidation.
items.thesis_assessment: The rates belief held: SOFR is 3.94, the US ten-year later printed 4.85 after a 22bp five-day rally, and December hike pricing firmed to about 44bp. The failed piece was adding dollar-franc when that pair was already near a one-year high beside a live euro short.
items.what_failed: The long dollar-franc was booked to extend a 20-day upside break while the US path stayed above the SOFR fixing. The break stopped extending and the swing was closed with dollar-franc still around 0.84, while the rate path stayed firm.
